title: ROOM AT GOD'S TABLE FOR THE OUTSIDER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'For the generations to come, whenever a foreigner or anyone else living among you presents a food offering as an aroma pleasing to the Lord, they must do exactly as you do. The community is to have the same rules for you and for the foreigner residing among you; this is a lasting ordinance for the generations to come. You and the foreigner shall be the same before the Lord: The same laws and regulations will apply both to you and to the foreigner residing among you.'" — Num 15:13-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Three times in these few verses God repeats the same wonderful truth: the foreigner living among Israel was welcome to worship on the very same terms as the native-born. "You and the foreigner shall be the same before the Lord." In a world where outsiders were usually shut out, God flung the door open.

This was remarkable for its time. God's people were never meant to be an exclusive club, hoarding His blessings for themselves. From the beginning, God's heart reached beyond Israel to the nations. The stranger who came to worship the true God was not treated as a second-class believer but was fully welcomed at His table.

There is comfort here for anyone who has ever felt like an outsider — like they do not belong, like the circle is closed to them. God's heart has always had room for those on the outside. He is not looking for people of the right pedigree, but for hearts that come to Him in worship and faith.

This foreigner-welcoming grace blossoms fully in the gospel. Through Christ, those who were once "foreigners and strangers" have been brought near and made fellow citizens with God's people. The dividing wall has been torn down. In Jesus, there is no longer outsider and insider — all who trust Him are brought into one family. If you have ever wondered whether there is a place for you with God, this ancient law whispers the answer, and the cross shouts it: yes, there is room for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you ever felt like an outsider to God's family?
2. How does God's welcome of the foreigner reveal His heart?
3. What does it mean to you that Christ has brought near those who were far off?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your heart has always had room for the outsider. Thank You that in Christ I who was once far off have been brought near and made part of Your family. Help me to welcome others as You have welcomed me. Amen.
